_note: T-EVAL systems-under-eval registry (Wave 9). Each entry points at the REAL prompt file under agent-config/ (injected via --append-system-prompt-file, exactly as K's synthesizer does), a degraded control prompt (omits the system's guardrail, to prove the metric discriminates), a rubric (LLM-judge criteria), and a cases JSON. allowedTools mirrors the tier/agent's real allowlist (minus Task for confinement and minus mcp__* servers not mounted in the throwaway sandboxes) so off-allowlist attempts surface as the enforcement signal.

systems.title: L0 base operating prompt
systems.job: the durable cross-tier rules injected beneath every K-managed run: plan-then-verify, use mounted skills, storage-is-tools, stay in the worktree, never reach the host config, minimal rooted changes, no push to a default branch, faithful reporting

systems.title: Secretary tier charter
systems.job: K the secretary — logistics, Q&A, scheduling, notes; routes every request and has NO code authority (no Bash/Write/Edit/Task); dispatches engineering to the Chief/an orchestrator and shows the route

systems.title: Orchestrator tier charter
systems.job: staff-engineer who runs the delegation loop (implementer -> review -> integrate), reports via the workflow status tool, ships ONE reviewable PR for the whole batch, branches first and NEVER pushes to a default branch, stops and re-plans if work goes sideways

systems.title: spec-reviewer worker
systems.job: reviews a diff against its brief + global constraints for EXACT spec compliance (nothing missing, nothing extra); read-only — flags, never fixes; emits a verdict + specific findings with file:line

systems.title: implementer worker
systems.job: builds exactly ONE task from a brief via TDD, verifies before claiming done (runs the tests, captures output), makes one focused commit, never pushes/PRs, never signs off its own work, reports status + concerns

systems.title: verification-before-completion skill
systems.job: the iron law — NO completion claims without fresh verification evidence: identify the proving command, RUN it, READ the output, only then claim; never trust 'should pass', a stale run, or a subagent's report
